raw_text:
Below is a 12-week strength program starting 2026-06-01, designed for an advanced 47-year-old female lifter in early perimenopause. It prioritizes bone-loading compound lifts, preserves/ builds muscle, manages heat intolerance, and includes structured cooling and recovery. It uses a 3-days-per-week full-body split with an optional low-heat conditioning day. Volume and intensity are periodized across three phases with a deload in Week 4 and Week 8 to manage recovery and thermoregulation.

Key principles
- Frequency: 3 full-body lifting days (Mon/Wed/Fri suggested). Optional low-heat conditioning on one other day (Tue or Sat).
- Bone-loading focus: Heavy axial and multi-planar compounds with progressive intensity: back/front squats, deadlift variants, overhead press, bench/weighted push-ups, weighted carries, step-ups, lunges, rows, pull-ups/chin-ups.
- Intensity and volume: Linear-to-wave progression. RPE guidance integrated. Two deloads.
- Heat management built-in: Session caps ~60–70 min including cooldown, longer rest on heavy sets, cold towel/ice pack between sets if needed, shaded/air-conditioned space only, post-session cooling protocol.
- Menstrual irregularity: Avoid tying cycles to programming; use autoregulation (RPE) and flexible load reductions on symptomatic hot days.
- Hypertrophy support: Accessory work targets hips, back, triceps, calves, core for posture and bone health.
- Power and impact: Low-to-moderate jump exposure for bone, scaled to tolerance; keep brief and in cool conditions.
- Conditioning: Zone 2 or low-impact intervals in cool environment; no fasted HIIT in heat.

Readiness and autoregulation
- Use RPE 6–9 for main lifts; reduce loads 2.5–7.5% on days with severe heat symptoms or poor sleep.
- Use longer rests (2–4 min compounds).
- If night sweats disrupted sleep, cap top-set RPE at 7–8 and skip optional sets.

Warm-up and cooldown every session
- Warm-up (10–12 min in cool environment)
  - 5 min brisk walk/airdyne/rower (cool room/fan).
  - Dynamic mobility: ankle rocks, hip airplanes, thoracic openers (2x6 each).
  - Movement prep with the day’s main patterns: 2–3 ramp-up sets for first two lifts.
- Between-set cooling options
  - Cold neck wrap or cooling towel; sip cool fluids.
  - Fans directed at lifter; chalk hands dry.
- Structured post-session cooling (8–10 min)
  - 5 min easy spin or walk with fan.
  - Cold pack on neck/upper back 5–8 min; cool shower as soon as feasible.
  - Rehydrate: 500–750 ml fluid with 300–500 mg sodium if sweaty; add 20–30 g protein if >3 hrs since last meal.

Nutrition (high level)
- Protein: 1.7–2.2 g/kg/day; distribution 3–4 feedings with 30–40 g high-leucine protein; 20–40 g within 1–2 hrs of training.
- Carbs: 3–5 g/kg/day baseline; 30–50 g within 60–90 min pre-lift for energy/thermoregulation; intra-session 15–30 g if sessions >60 min or heat symptoms rise.
- Fats: 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day.
- Creatine monohydrate 3–5 g/day; vitamin D3 per labs; calcium to 1,000–1,200 mg/day from food/supps; omega-3 1–2 g EPA+DHA/day.
- Hydration: 5–7 ml/kg in the 2 hrs pre-lift; sip cool electrolyte drink during; replace 125–150% of body mass lost within 4 hrs (weigh before/after in early weeks to estimate sweat rate).

Phase overview
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Accumulation and technical base; moderate loads, build tolerance. Week 4 deload.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Intensification; higher loads, modest volume. Week 8 deload.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Peak strength and power emphasis; lower volume, higher intensity; Week 12 is test/rep PR week.

Weekly template (Mon/Wed/Fri)
- Day A: Squat emphasis + overhead press + hinge accessory + pull
- Day B: Deadlift emphasis + bench/push + unilateral knee + vertical pull
- Day C: Front squat or split squat emphasis + press (alt) + posterior chain + row + carries
Optional Day D (cool environment): 20–35 min Zone 2 or low-impact tempo, mobility, breathwork.

Exercise pool (rotate as programmed)
- Squat patterns: Back squat (high-bar), front squat, safety bar squat, split squat variations, step-ups.
- Hinge: Conventional deadlift, trap bar deadlift, Romanian deadlift (RDL), hip hinge block pull.
- Press: Overhead press (barbell or DB), incline/flat bench press, weighted push-up.
- Pull: Pull-up/chin-up (weighted as able), lat pulldown, chest-supported row, single-arm row.
- Accessory bone-loading: Weighted carries (farmer/offset), sled push/pull (cool area), calf raises, tib raises, med-ball chest pass.
- Power/impact (brief): Low contacts of pogos, low box step-off to stick, med-ball slams. Omit on very hot days.

Load notation: Sets x reps @ RPE (or %1RM range if you prefer). If %s are used, default to RPE to autoregulate with heat.

PHASE 1: Weeks 1–4 (Accumulation; groove patterns; build volume; Week 4 deload)
- Goal: Establish consistent heavy axial loading without overheating. Moderate reps (5–8), RPE 6–8. Short, crisp sessions.

Week 1 (starting Mon 2026-06-01)
Day A
- Back squat: 4x6 @ RPE 7 (2–3’ rest)
- Overhead press: 4x5 @ RPE 7
- Romanian deadlift: 3x8 @ RPE 7
- Chest-supported row: 3x8 @ RPE 7
- Farmer carry: 3x30–40 m heavy, rest as needed
Day B
- Trap bar deadlift: 4x5 @ RPE 7
- Bench press: 4x6 @ RPE 7
- Reverse lunge (DB): 3x8/side @ RPE 7
- Pull-up or assisted: 4x4–6 @ RPE 7
- Standing calf raise: 3x10–12 @ RPE 7
Day C
- Front squat: 4x5 @ RPE 7
- Incline DB press: 3x8 @ RPE 7
- Hip thrust or glute bridge (barbell): 3x8 @ RPE 7
- One-arm DB row: 3x8/side @ RPE 7
- Suitcase carry (offset): 3x25–35 m/side

Week 2
- Progress load 2.5–5% if RPE ≤7 last week; keep reps.
Day A
- Back squat: 4x6 @ RPE 7–8
- Overhead press: 4x5 @ RPE 7–8
- RDL: 3x8 @ RPE 7–8
- Chest-supported row: 3x8 @ RPE 7–8
- Farmer carry: 4x30–40 m
Day B
- Trap bar deadlift: 5x4 @ RPE 7–8
- Bench press: 4x6 @ RPE 7–8
- Step-up (knee-high as tolerated): 3x8/side
- Pull-up: 4x5–6
- Calf raise: 3x12
Day C
- Front squat: 4x5 @ RPE 7–8
- Incline DB press: 3x8
- Hip thrust: 4x6–8 heavier
- One-arm DB row: 3x10/side
- Suitcase carry: 4x25–35 m/side

Week 3
- Slight rep reductions on top sets to raise intensity.
Day A
- Back squat: Top set 1x5 @ RPE 8, back-offs 3x5 @ -8–10% load
- Overhead press: 4x4 @ RPE 8
- RDL: 3x6–7 @ RPE 8
- Chest-supported row: 3x8 @ RPE 7–8
- Farmer carry: 3x40–50 m
Day B
- Trap bar deadlift: 1x4 @ RPE 8, 3x3 @ -8–10%
- Bench press: 1x5 @ RPE 8, 3x5 back-offs
- Reverse lunge: 3x6–7/side heavier
- Pull-up: 5x4–5 weighted if able
- Calf raise: 4x10
Day C
- Front squat: 4x4 @ RPE 8
- Incline DB press: 3x6–7 @ RPE 8
- Hip thrust: 3x6–7 @ RPE 8
- One-arm row: 3x8/side heavy
- Suitcase carry: 3x40 m/side

Week 4 (Deload)
- Reduce volume by ~40–50% and intensity to RPE 6–7. Keep movement patterns. Skip power/impact.
Day A: Back squat 3x4; OHP 3x4; RDL 2x6; Row 2x8; Farmer 2x25 m
Day B: Trap dead 3x3; Bench 3x4; Step-up 2x6/side; Pull-up 3x3; Calf 2x10
Day C: Front squat 3x3; Incline press 2x6; Hip thrust 2x6; 1-arm row 2x8; Suitcase 2x25 m

PHASE 2: Weeks 5–8 (Intensification; increase load; Week 8 deload)
- Goal: Heavier compounds, lower reps, preserve accessories for bone and posture. RPE 7–9.

Week 5
Day A
- Back squat: 5x4 @ RPE 8
- Overhead press: 5x3 @ RPE 8
- RDL: 3x5–6 @ RPE 8
- Chest-supported row: 4x6–8
- Farmer carry: 4x30–40 m heavy
Day B
- Conventional deadlift (switch from trap if desired): 4x3 @ RPE 8
- Bench press: 5x4 @ RPE 8
- Bulgarian split squat: 3x6/side heavy
- Weighted pull-up or chin-up: 5x3–5
- Standing calf raise: 4x8–10 heavy
Day C
- Front squat: 5x3 @ RPE 8
- Incline or close-grip bench: 4x5 @ RPE 8
- Hip thrust: 4x5–6 heavy
- 1-arm DB row: 4x6–8/side heavy
- Suitcase carry: 4x30–40 m/side

Week 6
- Introduce a top single/double at moderate-high RPE to keep skill under heavier load, followed by volume back-offs.
Day A
- Back squat: 1x2 @ RPE 8.5, then 4x3 @ -8–10%
- Overhead press: 1x2 @ RPE 8.5, then 4x3 @ -8–10%
- RDL: 3x5 @ RPE 8
- Row: 3x6–8
- Farmer: 3–4x40 m
Day B
- Deadlift: 1x2 @ RPE 8.5, then 3x3 back-offs
- Bench: 1x2 @ RPE 8.5, then 4x3 back-offs
- Bulgarian split squat: 3x6/side
- Weighted pull-up: 4x3–4
- Calf: 4x8–10
Day C
- Front squat: 1x2 @ RPE 8.5, then 4x3 back-offs
- Incline/close-grip bench: 4x4–5
- Hip thrust: 3x5–6
- 1-arm row: 3x6–8/side
- Suitcase carry: 3x40 m/side

Week 7
- Slight bump in volume at similar intensities; keep rests long, prioritize cooling.
Day A
- Back squat: 4x4 @ RPE 8–8.5
- Overhead press: 5x3 @ RPE 8–8.5
- RDL: 3x5 @ RPE 8–8.5
- Row: 4x6
- Farmer: 4x30–40 m heavy
Day B
- Deadlift: 4x3 @ RPE 8–8.5
- Bench: 4x4 @ RPE 8–8.5
- Step-up (higher box): 3x6/side
- Pull-up: 5x3–4 weighted
- Calf: 4x8–10
Day C
- Front squat: 5x3 @ RPE 8–8.5
- Incline/close-grip: 4x4 @ RPE 8–8.5
- Hip thrust: 3x5
- 1-arm row: 3x6–8
- Suitcase carry: 4x35–45 m

Week 8 (Deload)
- Intensity to RPE 6–7; volume -50%.
Day A: Back squat 3x3; OHP 3x3; RDL 2x5; Row 2x6; Farmer 2x25–30 m
Day B: Deadlift 3x2–3; Bench 3x3; Split squat 2x6/side; Pull-up 3x2–3; Calf 2x8
Day C: Front squat 3x2–3; Incline/close 2x4; Hip thrust 2x5; 1-arm row 2x6; Suitcase 2x25–30 m

PHASE 3: Weeks 9–12 (Peak strength + power; lower volume, higher intensity; Week 12 test/PRs)
- Goal: Maximize bone-stimulating heavy lifts with crisp technique; maintain cooling and auto-regulation. Add brief power primers at session start (cool room).

Power primers (Weeks 9–11; 5 min at start if feeling cool and fresh)
- Option A Day A: 3x3 low box jumps or pogos (low impact), long rest.
- Day B: 3x3 med-ball chest pass or slam.
- Day C: 3x3 seated vertical jump or split-stance med-ball throw.
- Skip on hot/symptomatic days.

Week 9
Day A
- Back squat: 1x1–2 @ RPE 8.5, then 3x2–3 @ -8–10%
- Overhead press: 1x1–2 @ RPE 8.5, then 3x2–3 back-offs
- RDL: 3x4–5 @ RPE 8
- Chest-supported row: 3x5–6 heavy
- Farmer: 3x40–50 m heavy
Day B
- Deadlift: 1x1–2 @ RPE 8.5, then 3x2 @ -8–10%
- Bench press: 1x1–2 @ RPE 8.5, then 3x2–3 back-offs
- Bulgarian split squat: 3x5/side
- Weighted pull-up: 4x2–3
- Calf raise: 3x6–8 heavy
Day C
- Front squat: 4x2–3 @ RPE 8–8.5
- Incline or close-grip: 4x3 @ RPE 8–8.5
- Hip thrust: 3x4–5 heavy
- 1-arm row: 3x5–6/side heavy
- Suitcase carry: 3x40–50 m/side

Week 10
- Slight load bump or hold and aim for tighter bar speed; same structure.
Day A
- Back squat: 1x1 @ RPE 9 (not a max), then 3x2 @ -8–10%
- Overhead press: 1x1 @ RPE 9, then 3x2 back-offs
- RDL: 3x4 @ RPE 8–8.5
- Row: 3x5–6
- Farmer: 3–4x40–50 m
Day B
- Deadlift: 1x1 @ RPE 9, then 3x2 back-offs
- Bench: 1x1 @ RPE 9, then 3x2–3
- Step-up heavy: 3x5/side
- Weighted pull-up: 4x2–3
- Calf: 3x6–8
Day C
- Front squat: 4x2 @ RPE 8.5
- Incline/close-grip: 4x2–3 @ RPE 8.5
- Hip thrust: 3x3–4 heavy
- 1-arm row: 3x5/side
- Suitcase carry: 3x40–50 m/side

Week 11
- Final heavy exposures; keep RPE 8.5–9; reduce accessories slightly.
Day A
- Back squat: 3x2 @ RPE 8.5–9
- Overhead press: 3x2 @ RPE 8.5–9
- RDL: 2x4 @ RPE 8
- Row: 2x5–6
- Farmer: 2–3x40 m
Day B
- Deadlift: 3x2 @ RPE 8.5–9
- Bench: 3x2 @ RPE 8.5–9
- Split squat: 2x5/side
- Weighted pull-up: 3x2
- Calf: 2x6–8
Day C
- Front squat: 3x2 @ RPE 8.5
- Incline/close: 3x2 @ RPE 8.5
- Hip thrust: 2x3–4
- 1-arm row: 2x5/side
- Suitcase carry: 2x40 m/side

Week 12 (Test/rep PRs or performance week; keep environment cool)
- Purpose: Assess progress with rep PRs at submax loads or conservative singles. Abort testing if heat symptoms spike; revert to Week 11 loads.
Day A (Squat + OHP test)
- Back squat: Work to 1x1 @ RPE 9 OR 3–5RM rep PR; then 2x3 @ ~85% of top set
- Overhead press: 1x1 @ RPE 9 OR 3–5RM rep PR; then 2x3 back-offs
- RDL: 2x4 @ RPE 8
- Row: 2x5–6
Day B (Deadlift + Bench test)
- Deadlift: Work to 1x1 @ RPE 9 OR 3–5RM rep PR; then 2x2–3 back-offs
- Bench press: 1x1 @ RPE 9 OR 3–5RM rep PR; then 2x3 back-offs
- Pull-up: 2x2–3 weighted or AMRAP bodyweight set if preferred
- Calf: 2x6–8
Day C (Front squat strength + carries)
- Front squat: 3–5RM; then 2x2–3 @ ~85%
- Incline/close-grip: 3x2–3 @ RPE 8
- Hip thrust: 2x3–4 heavy
- Suitcase carry: 2–3x40–50 m/side heavy

Optional low-heat conditioning (1x/week, Weeks 1–12)
- Zone 2: 20–35 min bike/row in 18–21°C room with fan; RPE 4–5. Or 10x1 min brisk incline walk, 1 min easy.
- Finish with breathing: 3–5 min nasal 4-6 breathing in cool room to downshift.

Mobility and bone health extras (2–3x/week, short blocks)
- Ankles/calves, hips (90/90 switches, hip airplanes), T-spine rotations, loaded carries (already in plan), and brief pogo drills on cool days.
- Posture and core: Pallof press 2x10/side, dead bug 2x6/side, side plank 2x20–30s/side on lighter days.

Heat-intolerance playbook
- Train only in AC or shaded mornings/evenings; bring two chilled bottles and a cooling towel.
- If hot flashes escalate mid-session:
  - Pause 3–5 min, apply cool pack to neck, sip electrolytes.
  - Drop next sets by one rep or reduce load 2.5–5%.
  - If not relieved, stop compound lift and move to accessories or end with cooldown.
- Avoid: sauna exposure; fasted HIIT; outdoor midday sessions.

Monitoring and progression
- Track: RPEs, loads, symptoms (hot flashes 0–10), sleep, cycle dates, and session temps.
- Adjust: If two consecutive sessions reach RPE >9 early, add an extra rest day or swap to deload-style volume for that week’s remaining sessions.
- Aim to progress main lifts 2.5–5% across Phases 1–2, then secure quality doubles/singles in Phase 3.

Safety and technique notes
- Emphasize bracing, neutral spine; controlled eccentrics (2–3 s) on squats/presses in Phases 1–2 for bone stimulus.
- Footwear: stable shoes for squats/presses; straps allowed on heavy rows/RDLs as needed to protect grip for carries.
- Weighted pulls and carries are potent bone-loading tools; keep them heavy but technically clean.

This structure gives you a clear week-by-week plan with bone-centric compound loading, sensible progression, and explicit cooling protocols suited to early perimenopause and heat intolerance. Adjust exercise selections to available equipment while preserving the pattern and loading intent.
